newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real seesaws, ends off 0.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real seesaws, ends off 0.25 pct.

text.p: The Brazilian real fell 0.25 percent to close at 1.0742 per dollar in seesaw trade in the commercial foreign exchange market due to dollar outflows, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $45 million surplus on Wednesday, but dealers were certain that at the end of the day the total would swing to a deficit.
The Central Bank sold dollars at 1.0740 reais in the late afternoon to satisfy market demand, dealers said.
Despite a $982 million surplus on Tuesday, dealers said the market did not benefit from the dollar inflow as some $800 million were sold directly to the Central Bank.
Players are expecting a new decline in the real-dollar mini-band on Friday. The market will be closed Thursday for the Corpus Christi holiday.

The current mini-band was set on Monday at 1.0690 to 1.0740 the dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.52 percent against the dollar compared to an average drop of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past four months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0746 per dollar, down 0.02 percent. In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.18 percent to end at 1.132 per dollar.
